not_covered.topic: South Korea–United States relations, Japan–United States relations
not_covered.text: The South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff confirms that the annual Freedom Edge trilateral military exercises between the United States, South Korea, and Japan will go on as scheduled between September 7 and 11.
Three Palestinians are reported to be killed in strikes in the Gaza Strip, violating the October 2025 ceasefire.

The Israel Defense Forces and its Spokesperson's Unit confirms Al-Qassam Brigades commander Ismail Mohammad Ibrahim Barim, who held Edan Alexander, Matan Zangauker, and Avera Mengistu as hostages, was killed in a strike in Khan Yunis.

The IDF also confirms that they have recently killed two Hamas militants that invaded the Re'im Base in Re'im during the October 7 attacks in separate strikes in the Gaza Strip, including a body guard to former leader Yahya Sinwar and a Nuk
It is reported that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has held secret meetings with Hamas during the 2014 Gaza War. The Prime Minister's Office denies the reports.
Four people are killed after an unconfirmed civilian or military airplane is shot down with a surface-to-air missile near Minembwe, Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Sudan's army repels a Rapid Support Forces attack on the town of Al-Keli in the Blue Nile region.
Around 12 people are reported killed in a airstrike near border with Chad.
Around 49 people are killed in a cattle raid on the Machar-Pakuek cattle camp in Mading Juer Boma in Tonj North County of South Sudan's Warrap state.
A section of the Trans-Canada Highway in the Fraser Canyon reopens after being closed for seven weeks due to the wildfires.

The United States Geological Survey says a glacial collapse and debris flow, not an earthquake, caused the seismic event near the Nepal–Tibet border and subsequent flooding that killed at least 392 people and left over 900 more missing.
U.S. officials report that 90 Americans have been reported missing since the floods, with the U.S. State Department reporting that three have been rescued.

Tropical Storm Dolly forms in the Atlantic Ocean. The World Meteorological Organization clarifies there is no connection between the storm's name and to the death of former American country singer Dolly Parton, being merely coincidental.
The death toll from the earthquake that struck the Flores island in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, rises to 111, with 176,000 people displaced.
The X2 roller coaster at the Six Flags Magic Mountain amusement park in Valencia, California, U.S., closes after two riders were recently hospitalized for brain injuries including hemorrhages.
Six people die after a pump boat carrying 13 passengers capsizes while crossing the Mapanuepe Lake in San Marcelino, Zambales, Philippines. Three others remain missing.

Germany's Robert Koch Institute estimates 15,800 heat-related deaths during summer 2026, the highest total in a decade of monitoring, as repeated heat waves push temperatures above {{convert|40|C|F}}. .
Two people are killed in a stabbing at a private school in Gosen-Neu Zittau, Brandenburg, Germany. A suspect is arrested.

not_covered.topic: Ethnic cleansing in the Bosnian War

Zambian presidential candidate Brian Mundubile surrenders to police and is questioned over an alleged national security threat after two weeks in hiding following the disputed presidential election, in which he finished second.
The Korea AeroSpace Administration says that the Nuri will launch 15 satellites, a record, into space from the Naro Space Center in South Korea's Goheung County on October 7.
A near-total partial lunar eclipse occurs over the Americas, Africa and Europe.

Brazilian Alison dos Santos and American Masai Russell breaks the world records in men's 400 metres (45.80 seconds) and women's 100 metres hurdles (12.09 seconds), respectively, at the 2026 Weltklasse Zürich in Zurich, Switzerland.
